The queue holds up to 100 jobs. Leases control when a job becomes available again; only explicit acknowledgement removes it.

1. **Capacity is 100 jobs.** This sets the queue’s maximum job count.
2. **Jobs beyond capacity are rejected.** Rejection makes the failure explicit instead of silently dropping work.
3. **A running job has a 30-second lease.** This gives the job a limited period before it becomes available again unless the lease is renewed.
4. **Workers renew leases every 10 seconds.** Renewal keeps the lease active while the worker processes the job.
5. **An expired lease makes the job available again.** Work can be picked up again when its lease is no longer maintained, but this also permits another run of the same job.
6. **Handlers must be idempotent because a job can run twice.** Repeating a job must not repeat its effects incorrectly. Lease expiry and renewed availability are why handlers must tolerate duplicate runs.
7. **Only explicit acknowledgement removes a job.** Renewal maintains the lease; expiry restores availability. Neither removes the job. Acknowledgement is the separate action that removes it.
